YouTube description seed: Ever noticed the cut lines at a stop line? Guess what's inside. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: An inductive loop of wire buried in the road detects the metal of a car above it.
The later surprise: Small bikes may not have enough metal to trigger it.
The very first frame shows a car rolling up to a red light and stopping on sealed saw-cut lines in the asphalt. Nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
Hook test: A (statement) = "This traffic light knows you're waiting."; B (question) = "How does a red light know a car is there?".
Fact boundaries: Say 'many' lights; others use cameras or radar. Do not say bikes never trigger them. The main reveal lands in scene 4.

facts.statement: Inductive loop detectors are wire coils set in the pavement; a vehicle's metal changes the loop's inductance and signals the controller.
Bicycles and small motorcycles may fail to trigger loops because they contain little metal.
